image_description: A large sturgeon swimming in an aquarium tank, viewed through glass. The fish has a dark gray/brown body with visible bony scutes along its side and back. The head is elongated with a pointed snout, though the ventral mouth and barbels are obscured by the viewing angle. The tail appears heterocercal. The background shows a sandy bottom and another fish in the distance.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Four barbels (sensory whiskers) anterior to mouth.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Barbels are located on the ventral side of the snout. Due to the camera angle looking slightly down at the side of the fish, the underside of the head is not visible, rendering this feature untestable.
The snout is clearly visible extending forward in a tapered, pointed shape consistent with sturgeon morphology.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elongated fusiform body with impressively large, extended proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body is distinctly elongated and torpedo-shaped (fusiform), occupying a significant portion of the frame, matching the description.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Distinct rows of raised, bony plates (scutes) are clearly visible running longitudinally along the flank and dorsal ridge of the fish. No typical fish scales are present.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Gray, brown, or black dorsally with lighter ventral surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal side is dark gray/brown. While the full ventral side is hard to see, the lower flank transitions to a significantly lighter, pinkish-tan color, consistent with the counter-shading described.
The caudal fin is clearly visible and exhibits the characteristic asymmetry of a heterocercal tail, with the upper lobe being larger and extending further than the lower lobe.
